utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you like to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, your Honour. Before the Prosecution calls the first witness, I would like to attempt -- I see Mr. Wladimiroff is up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, I am just waiting.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He cannot wait! He is ready. Very good. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would like to attempt to clarify a misunderstanding that may have arisen yesterday and I think needs attention. The witness who testified yesterday was asked during cross-examination whether or not he was shown a photograph of the accused when he was interviewed by German authorities. The suggestion in context was clearly that his identification of the accused was based on the fact that he was previously shown a photograph of the accused rather than being based on a lifetime of growing up in the same village with the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: But you asked him how many photos he had seen, as I recall -- I have not reviewed the transcript -- and it was 13 or 14 or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct. We do have the copy of the German record of the display of photographic array that was shown to the witness and we have the photo book with us which clearly discloses that the witness was shown a book which contained 24 photographs of similar looking individuals, and that he clearly recognised the photograph of the accused Dusko Tadic among those photographs and selected them from among all those photographs. So, the actual interview proceeding clearly stands for the opposite of what was suggested in court and I think it needs to be brought to the attention of the court. If the court desires, we have that document and can certainly tender it to the court for its review.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff? Do you have anything to say regarding that issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. We will object to the tendering of these photographs. I am not sure we have got them all. We may have some because we got the German file from the German lawyer and on occasions we found that it was not complete so I am not sure we have the same photographs here. But, principally, we object to the tendering of those photographs for the very reasons I have given you two days ago. I think we first have to be clear what is the probative value of such photospread before it could be tendered, so we object to that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It would not be appropriate if we were to apply strict, certainly, rules of evidence for the photographs to be tendered in the form that you are suggesting. If you were going to tender them, you would have to do that through the witness. Of course, that raises the issue that we thought we did not have to consider until several witnesses away. This witness though, however, testified, as I recall, that he had known Tadic, had seen Tadic. I recall also in cross-examination that you put to this witness that Mr. Tadic did not know him, so I do not know what evidence is going to be offered at a particular point in time. Mr. Wladimiroff, you along with the written statement that you made in court two days ago, you submitted something which I have not reviewed actually but you had said that it was a submission from Dr. Wagenaar. I do not know how we will consider that even without hearing from Dr. Wagenaar. We had not decided at least, and we still have not decided, whether we are going to hear from Dr. Wagenaar before we even rule on that issue. So what I am trying to say is that all of this is up in the air at this point. I would suggest that we forget about the photos that you are suggesting, the 24 photos, unless you want to recall the witness. If you wish to recall the witness, then we will have to deal with these issues that we were putting off for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I understand what the court is saying. If I may, before I conclude, just remind the court of the context in which this arose. These were not presented by the Prosecution to show a further basis for recognition. We were content to wait until the resolution of this issue. The Defence, however, chose to suggest to the court that this witness had been tainted by a procedure which, in fact, demonstrates the witness's ability to recognise the defendant, because in a booklet of numerous photos he was able to pick him out when the suggestion by the Defence was quite the contrary. I think that is a different matter than the Prosecution stepping forward trying to prematurely raise this issue before the resolution of the matter that we had previously discussed. That is why I raise it today.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Judge Stephen has pointed me to the portion of the transcript -- that is on page 1925 -- where it is at least discussed on redirect, as I recall. Is there anything that you wish from the Trial Chamber at this point with respect to that testimony other than to make this statement, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the light of the court's response -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I know you wish us to accept everything that you have said, but is there any action required by us at this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, nothing other than I was going to tender the documents. I understand the court's response to that so I have nothing beyond that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, very good. Mr. Wladimiroff, do you have an additional matter or something further than this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No other additional matter, your Honour. The Trial Chamber ruled on our motion on the protection of witnesses on May 7th. It would be very convenient for us if we could have the written version before we leave for Bosnia. I am just drawing your attention to the fact that we have not received that so far.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Just this morning I have seen the decision that is in the process of translation. You understand that it has to be translated into French before it is issued, but you will receive that before you leave for Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you like to call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. The Prosecution's next witness is Nihad Haskic. MR. NIHAD HASKIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take that oath that is before you? THE WITNESS (In Translation): I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, what is your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nihad Haskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what year were you born?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is your nationality or ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you raised in Prijedor? Did you grow up there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I grew up in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did you go to school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Trnopolje, the first four grades, and the rest was in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you perform compulsory service with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I served in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in 73 and 74.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After performing your compulsory service did you return to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had you been trained in auto mechanics and did you work in car repair and sales after your return to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In 1979 did you open a business, a different kind of business?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I opened a kebab shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Kebab is a food speciality, a meat speciality, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Banja Luka grill.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was your kebab shop a popular and well known shop in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In 1986 did you start a construction firm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did that firm specialise in laying telephone phone cables?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So you worked with the PTT, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, during the time you were growing up in Prijedor how were relations between the ethnic groups in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were good.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know Dule Tadic before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he know you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did the two of you happen to know each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We came to know each other. His was a prominent family, Tadic's, karate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So he was a fairly well known person in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the whole family.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you well known as the owner of the kebab shop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If you do not mind, can you tell the court what your nickname was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cevap.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Dule Tadic well known enough so that if he came to your shop and you were not there, your wife might mention to you that he had visited the shop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was your wife from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hrnici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did she know Dule Tadic well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you and Dule Tadic met in the street would you greet each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, only "Hi, hi".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would you ever chat a bit, for example, would he mention that he had been to your shop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes he would say, "Your grilled meat is OK", and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see him many times from the time you opened your shop until the outbreak of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say how many times. I do not remember, but on various occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would you say a few times or many times that you encountered Dule Tadic and saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Quite a number of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What size was Dule Tadic? What kind of build did he have? How big a man was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule Tadic was on the short side but he was very well, very stolid, very sturdily built.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he sometimes have a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he sometimes not have a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes he had it and sometimes he did not. He did not always have a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Haskic, I would like to ask you a few questions about the period of time before the war. First, do you recall when the takeover of Prijedor occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the night between 29th and 30th April in early morning hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had there been any political tensions which preceded the takeover that people in the area were generally aware of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the takeover come as a surprise to you and your friends and family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you in Prijedor on the morning that the takeover had occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did you see in Prijedor that morning? What was the situation in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The situation in Prijedor, there were very many soldiers and there were military and the police in front of every important building and there were check points; and flags had been hoisted in all the buildings in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What kind of flags?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb flags.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there armed soldiers in the area and positioned in particular places?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there any snipers in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Snipers were on the tops of the buildings, on the roofs of the buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you able to go to work that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not because those at the PTT, had told me to stop with my work, to discontinue my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After that takeover did the situation for Muslims continue to deteriorate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It deteriorated drastically.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were Muslims losing their jobs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they at physical risk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and it grew worse with every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you send your family away from the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did on 15th May.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was that the last opportunity for people to leave the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the last convoy of buses which left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After that did the attempt to travel run the risk of physical harm to any Muslim who attempted it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had the radio or television broadcast changed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we could only watch Serbian television programme from then on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you aware when the attacks on Hambarine and Kozarac occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did you learn about those attacks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We watched the attacks on Hambarine. We watched it as it is very near Prijedor, and about the attack on Kozarac, I heard from the refugees from Kozarac in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You say "the refugees", some of the people from Kozarac fled to Prijedor after the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the attack there was a flow of refugees which reached Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When did the cleansing of Prijedor begin, Prijedor town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ethnic cleansing of Prijedor began on Saturday, on May 30th.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was at home then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What neighbourhood in Prijedor town did you live in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived in the part of Prijedor called Zagrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What ethnic group lived in that neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That part they were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did you first know that day, on May 30th, that something was happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I learnt it by hearing early morning gunfire and then Radio Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was it you heard on Radio Prijedor? What were you told was occurring?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We heard that Prijedor had been attacked and that we should stay at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were Muslims and Croats directed to do anything other than stay at home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were told to stay at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they told to do anything else while they were at home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During that day they also said to hoist white flags on the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you hoist a white flag or hang a white sheet out of your window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did many of your neighbours do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Many did and many did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After hearing the radio broadcast and the sounds of gunfire, did you stay home for a portion of the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In addition to hearing gunfire, did you also hear the sound of shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: From your house could you see any portions of Prijedor being shelled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could see part of the old town which was being shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What ethnic group lived in Stari Grad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were you able to see was happening in Stari Grad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we could see a tank arrive and shell houses and how they went to put houses on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was the tank going from house to house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At some point during the day did you leave your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why did you leave your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I thought that that might be safer, that it would be better if I were among the crowd, one of the crowd.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to my neighbour's.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could have this map marked as Prosecution Exhibit 229 for identification, please?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It will be 230, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour, I am sorry. Mr. Haskic, do you recognise this map as showing portions of Prijedor town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do. I do recognise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you find the vicinity of your neighbourhood on that map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 230 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we place that on the elmo for a moment? Mr. Haskic, can you point out on this map where your house was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If you could do so on the actual document itself which is to your right, we will all be able to see it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here. (The witness indicated on the map).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you show us where the house of the neighbour, where you went during the day is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here. (The witness indicated on the map).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Perhaps I can ask you to mark those places with a pen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked on the map).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is there also a mosque in that neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is. The mosque was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You can take your seat again. Did you remain in your neighbour's house for a period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did your neighbour also have a garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did other people from the neighbourhood gather at your neighbour's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you and those others from your neighbourhood stay in the house during some portions of the day, in the garage during other portions of the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you able to see from your neighbour's house what was happening in Stari Grad or any other adjacent neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could see what was happening in Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the destruction of houses that you spoke of earlier continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the whole day, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At some point did Serb troops reach your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did they do when they first came into your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were shooting and saying, "Everybody come out".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they shouting that? How were they saying that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One had a kind of an amplifier, a voice amplifier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you recall what that soldier was ordering people using the amplifier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was saying, "Come out. We will kill you".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the Serb troops entered and you were all ordered to come out, did you and the others all leave the garage or house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We came out of the garage and come out into the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were the Serb troops who came into your neighbourhood wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They all had weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they in uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What kinds of uniforms did they have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they wearing anything on their heads?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They had bright red beret hats.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there any emblems or insignias on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had Serb insignia on their arms, around their arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, in addition to you and the others who had been in the garage, did other people from the neighbourhood gather in the street in response to the orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We all came out, the whole town came out into the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you show us using the plan where you were directed to go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were told to go towards the town.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is the map still on the elmo? 230?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, perhaps you can use that pointer and, turning to the map to your right, show us where you and the others went?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went here towards the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So you went from the area of the garage up your street in the direction of the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see what was happening at your own house when you walked up your block toward the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I was passing by my house, I saw that it was burning, it was all in flames.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were any other houses on the block also burning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Across from my house there were two houses that were burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you walked up the block did you observe whether or not any of your neighbours were killed on the spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to the right Fuad Ekimovic was shot and was killed in his backyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So he was still in his yard when he was shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: He had not come out into the street as ordered by the Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You have pointed out or you have shown us on the map where the mosque was located. Did anything happen to the mosque that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day the mosque was hit by a shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was the minaret still standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The minaret was -- half of it was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did the group of Muslims from the neighbourhood stop as you walked up the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It stopped up there in front of a plateau where the buildings were and this is where the buses were waiting for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you show us on the map where that position was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is here. (The witness indicated on the map).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Perhaps you can also mark that with a pen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked on the map).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Are there any buildings in that area where the group stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are a cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What kind of buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Buildings where the SDK Bank was, then there was another bank a little bit further, PBS Bank from Sarajevo, and there was also a building where people lived and then underneath on the ground floor there was a co-operative.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You say there was buses waiting when you arrived. What happened to the group of Muslims from your neighbourhood when you arrived at that spot where the buses were waiting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were loaded on the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were some people loaded on some buses and other people loaded on others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Men were loaded on the buses and women and children were moved away to the other side, separated to the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there also elderly men among the group of people who had been marched up the street to that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were the elderly men placed when the separation occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Into the same buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The buses with the men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you taken after you boarded the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were taken to the centre of the town in front of the hotel, Balkan Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did you see there when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were there in the buses. We were not coming out, but we saw that from all over the city, the town, the buses were coming to this point, to that spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On your way from the location where you had been placed on the bus to the area of Hotel Balkan, did you see any bodies in the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw to the left of the market there were corpses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After being taken to the area of Hotel Balkan, where many other buses came, where were the buses then taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a column and then we started moving and we were stopped in front of the SUP building. The column was stopped in front of the SUP building.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is the police building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did policemen come on the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not into my bus but into other buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were some people taken off the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened to those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those people after a certain time were returned to the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had any of them been beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About how long were the buses at the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you exactly, it looked like eternity. It was not long. They did not stay there long.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know what was happening at that point to you and the others? Did you know what was intended for you or where you were going to go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not know. I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did the buses then go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The buses went on and were taking us on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you were being transported, were you and the other prisoners ordered to sit on the buses in a particular way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were. We were supposed to put our heads down and not watch where we were moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did your bus end up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then my bus came to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About what time of the day was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you got off the bus at Omarska what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took us out and they were -- we were made to stand against the wall and they would search us and take everything that we had on us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were any of the new prisoners beaten at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. During the search some people were hit, some were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In addition to having your documents and valuables taken, were your names recorded when you first got there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all names were recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That night in what part of Omarska camp did you stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That night I stayed at the entrance by the restaurant, by a room by the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Inside the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Next to the restaurant, a room next to the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to look at that model and can you just point out the building you were in that night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. How long did you stay in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed in that room for a very short time, one night.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then were you moved to another room in the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, at that time I went on to pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you point out using the model where the pista is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is this pista. (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: While you were staying on the pista, did you remain there all day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did, we slept there on the pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you sometimes sleep in any other portion of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did. While we were on the pista, one night I spend in the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you placed in a particular room in the white house along with other prisoners from the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was placed with the detainees who came with me from the pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: While you were in the white house did you have an opportunity to see any of the rooms other than the one in which you were placed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I entered I saw two rooms at the front part of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the condition of those rooms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the left of the room to the left, I saw two people lying on the, on the tiles, on the concrete.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see anything on the floor or the walls?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the walls and on the floor there was an old blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Approximately how long did you stay on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the pista I stayed altogether about nine or 10 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you held after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that I was transferred to the room in hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could ask for some assistance from Mr. Bos, perhaps we can remove those top portions of the hangar building so we can see the inside? Mr. Haskic, can I ask you to take a look at the model and see if you can locate the room in which you were held after the pista and you may get up to do so? If you do see it, will you please point to it and then I will ask you to identify the number of the room. I might mention to you that there are numbers on the model that are just numbers used for the court's benefit. They do not correspond to any of the numbers that were used for the rooms in the camp. So if you can get up, take a look at the model and tell us if you can see the room in which you were located, please point it out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot see from this side. Here. (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Can you see that, Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Hardly.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Why do you not stand up so you can see also?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: It is very difficult to see. I think if the light is a little bit low, then the screen is not that wide.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Point one more time, sir. Mr. Haskic, would you point one more time to the room where you were held and, Mr. Wladimiroff, if you want to stand up so you can get a better view, you may.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We cannot hear the witness as he is not speaking into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That room was No. 15. The entrance was here. Here, this is the room. This is the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Haskic, can you see the number or numbers which are on the model in this room and, if so, can you just tell us what they are?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you eventually moved from that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After interrogation I returned to the original room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you remain in that room in the restaurant building until you left Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mentioned your interrogation. Did you know any of the interrogators in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did you happen to know them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew them from the town because they were all from the police, from SUP in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who some of those interrogators were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was interrogated by Zjelko Tomcic -- Neso Tomcic and Neso Babic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did Neso Tomcic and Neso Babic do before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were officers, active police officers, inspectors in SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall any other persons who were interrogators in Omarska and who you knew from before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember Drago Meakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did Drago Meakic do before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same, he was also an inspector, a SUP inspector.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was he active or retired immediately before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war, just before the war he retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What other interrogators do you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember Obrad Despotovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did he do before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also an inspector with SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Any others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rade Teic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was he also associated with the SUP before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see these inspectors, these former inspectors, who were now interrogators in Omarska arriving at camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How often would they come to camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every day, they were coming in the morning by buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About what time would they leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would leave in the afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether prisoners were beaten during the interrogations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see the conditions of these prisoners before and after their interrogations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After interrogation many -- not many -- all of them were severely beaten up. They were black all over.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you describe the conditions in Omarska while you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The conditions in Omarska were intolerable. We all contracted typhoid, dysentery, we had lice. There was daily ill-treatment. People even slept in toilets. We were fed only one eighth of a loaf of bread and a couple of spoonfuls of some liquid called "soup" in a plate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you provided with drinking water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did have drinking water, but that water was not used before the war as this was not good water, since it has a high content of iron ore but we drank it there, nevertheless.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were women also held in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were they held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They spent days in the restaurant where we had our meals.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not there were any women held in the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In addition to the beatings which prisoners suffered during interrogations, were prisoners beaten at other times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat us whenever they could.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were prisoners beaten on the way to their meal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, then they would line up and we had to pass between those two lines, between two rows of them, and as we went through they beat us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were prisoners beaten when they attempted to use the toilet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As one would go into and come out of the toilet, yes, they sometimes would hit the prisoners or sometimes we hesitated to go to the toilet because we knew that somebody would be beaten there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did prisoners, many of whom were suffering from dysentery, find other ways to relieve themselves rather than using the toilets where they might be beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were in the hangar, in room 15. There one could wash one's hands, but some people did relieve themselves there only to avoid going to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were prisoners called out at night from various portions of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you able to hear what was sometimes happening to those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could only see some of them when they would be brought back into the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was their condition when they returned to the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Badly beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did some prisoners fail to return after being called out of their rooms at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Many did not return.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How regularly were people called out from the rooms and failed to return?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were called out every night.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see corpses in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them on the grass when we were on the pista, on the grass near the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would you see them in the morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would the corpses then be removed at some point during the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At times they would stay there for a day or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, were you taken to Manjaca after leaving Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we went to Manjaca, the first night we spent on the bus. We did not enter the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Eventually after arriving in Manjaca, were you weighed by the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Red Cross examined us only a couple of days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was your weight when arriving in Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 51 kilogrammes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was your weight before coming to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 83 kilogrammes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any Serbian officials from Prijedor other than the SUP inspectors or former SUP inspectors coming to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The head of the SUP from Prijedor used to come, Simo Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How often did Drljaca come to Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How frequently did Drljaca come to Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could see that, that is, I could see him several times as I was on the pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know Simo Drljaca before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We played football together and I knew him from my restaurant. He regularly came there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you saw him in Omarska camp did he come to the camp with anyone else from outside the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty soldier of the former JNA, Milovan Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Simo Drljaca with members of the camp administration -- with the camp Commander, for example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was the Commander of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zelko Mejakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have this marked for identification? It is a still photograph taken from a video which is already in evidence which is No. 184.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be 231, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, that is correct. Mr. Haskic, do you recognise the persons shown in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who is shown in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this photograph, Simo Drljaca to the right and Milovan Milutinovic is next to him on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Could that photograph be placed on the monitor, please?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to 231?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Using your pointer, sir, can you first point out Simo Drljaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now point out Milovan Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether or not Serbian officials from outside Prijedor ever visited the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once while I was on the pista a helicopter arrived, but I did not see who was on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you told by anyone what the purpose of the helicopter visit was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As detainees, we could only guess, but none of the guards told us anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Haskic, you have told us about prisoners being regularly taken from rooms and being beaten. During the time you were in Omarska, do you recall an incident when Emir Beganovic and Senad Muslimovic were called from your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do. They were with me in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Which room were you in at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time I was in the hangar on the upper floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What time of the day approximately were they called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember the approximate date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was on June 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall who was called out first?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think Beganovic was called out first.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see his condition after he returned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was his condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Appalling.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he have any visible injuries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a very visible injury. There was a cut on his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Could you see other signs that he had been beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was black all over when he took off his clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was Muslimovic's condition when he returned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslimovic's condition was better than Beganovic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had he also been badly beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but less than Beganovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had you heard the sounds of beating or sounds of pain or screams from the prisoners when Beganovic and Muslimovic had been called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All we could hear were cries of pain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After Beganovic and Muslimovic had been called out and beaten, did you hear screams from other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we heard terrible screams.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is there any way to describe those screams?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is beyond description. They were horrible. Your blood froze in your veins when you heard those screams.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were those screams coming from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those screams came from below us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: From the ground floor of the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from the ground floor of the hangar, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long did the screams of the prisoners last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not say, to us it looked like eternity. I do not know how long.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you later learn which prisoners had been called out and whose screams you had heard on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We learned that the next day when we went to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who were the prisoners whose screams you had heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We heard that it had been Eno Alic, Jasmin Hrnic and Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know Karabasic's first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Emir Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know these men from before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did Emir Karabasic do before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Emir was an active duty policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did Eno Alic do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Alic was a driver in a company, a truck driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did Jasmin Hrnic do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jasmin Hrnic had his own business, shipping business, delivery.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What part of Prijedor were these men from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, Jasmin was from Hrnici and the other two were from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Are you related to Jasmin Hrnic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is my wife's brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you and your family managed to escape from Bosnia, did you and your family make efforts to find out if Jasmin Hrnic was still alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We tried all we could through all possible organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you make every possible contact with every organisation that might have information about his whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you contact people, refugees, in various countries to find out if they had any knowledge of Jasko's whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did any international agency have any record of Jasmin Hrnic surviving the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had any survivor of Omarska or refugee from the area of Prijedor seen Jasmin Hrnic alive after he was taken to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After Omarska? I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I will rephrase that. Had anyone whom you attempted to contact seen Jasmin alive since the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mentioned the date of June 18th. Is there any particular reason why you are able to remember that date, or that you recall that date as being the date of the incident in which Muslimovic and Beganovic were called out and heard the screams from downstairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because that morning I learnt about that thing, about what had happened, and it simply remained imprinted in my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Haskic, during the time you were in Omarska camp, did you ever see Dule Tadic in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On how many occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him twice -- no, three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see him with your own eyes on three occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Twice I saw him with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you the first time you saw Dule Tadic in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time I was on the pista then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So that would have been in the early part of June shortly after you arrived at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened while I was on the pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Using the pointer, can you show us on the model where you were on the pista when you saw Dule Tadic on this first occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model) Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So approximately in the middle part of the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that a little toward the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you standing, sitting or lying down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that particular moment we were sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there occasions while you were on the pista when prisoners were forced to lie down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When would that occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it happened when some strange things would happen in the camp, then we would be ordered to lie down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there occasions while you were on the pista when prisoners who were sitting down were ordered to look down to the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there times when prisoners on the pista were sitting down and did not have orders to either look to the ground or lie down on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At times we could look around freely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On this occasion, the first time you saw Dule Tadic, which direction were you facing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was facing towards the end, towards the corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you facing the hangar building or restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were facing the canteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was Dule Tadic when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule Tadic was here. (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That would be at the corner of the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the corner of this building here. (The witness indicated on the model) The hangar is across the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So that would be the corner of the menza building which is closest to you, the front corner, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this corner here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did anything in particular draw your attention to that area or did you just look over and see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a rumour spread that Dule had come to the camp. Among the inmates the rumour was spread.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you saw him there, was he alone or with others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was a group.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Approximately how many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, three or four. That was a group.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall what the people in that group were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were they doing when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how long they remained there in that corner of the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see where they went after they left that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They went towards the restaurant, towards the canteen. (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the time that Dule Tadic and the others were standing in the spot you indicated, were you staring at them constantly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you looking up and then looking away so that you would not be seen by Dule Tadic or any of the guards looking at him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We just cast a glance so as not to be noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know exactly how many times you looked at him or for how long a period you looked at him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say for how long and how many times but, at any rate, enough to know that it was him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On the second occasion when you saw Dule Tadic, where were you sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second time I was sitting near to this side. (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So you were toward one side of the pista, the side of the pista away from the white house, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Approximately in the middle of the pista, that is, approximately between the hangar and the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Which direction were you facing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were facing, facing the canteen again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On this occasion where was Dule Tadic when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule Tadic was here.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It would help if you could focus on the area where the witness points. Mr. Tieger, would you ask him to point again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Haskic, if you could indicate with the pointer once again where Dule Tadic was when you saw him on this second occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here. (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Again you have indicated a position next to the restaurant building ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- on the corner furthest from the white house and across from the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For the purposes of clarification, your Honour, the first time the witness was asked where he was sitting, it did not come up on the video monitor. I wonder if that might be indicated so that we could see it on our screens?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you do that quickly, please, and then we will stand in recess? The reason, Mr. Tieger, is that the view is obstructed of the Defence. They cannot see over the exhibit. That is why I ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I appreciate that. Mr. Haskic, I want to return for a moment, if I may, to the first occasion when you saw Dule Tadic in camp.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the first occasion he was here on the corner and on the second occasion he was a bit nearer to that place over there. (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you show us with the pointer where you were on the first occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On this occasion I was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Approximately in the middle of the pista then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It looks like the model -- it is not my eyes, is it? No. Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. For explanation, your Honour, as you noted, the model is tilted. That is so it will aid the camera view. Mr. Haskic, we have the benefit of some additional equipment which will enable both the court and all the attorneys in the courtroom to see the areas which you previously indicated. So, I am going to ask you to once again indicate some of the areas you showed us before. When you point them out, I will ask you to do so slowly so the camera can catch it and so that everyone in the courtroom can see where that is. I realise that will probably involve you getting up and down a couple of times, but I ask for your help with that. First of all, sir, can I ask you to show us once again the part of the hangar you were in when Beganovic and Muslimovic were called out and on that occasion when you heard the screams coming from the ground floor of the hangar, the part of the camp you were in at that time, if you could show us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in room No. 15, here. (The witness indicated on the model) Exactly here. Exactly here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As we looked at that area, it showed a fairly large area with two smaller rooms or areas within it. What were those two areas inside that larger area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those two areas to the left was the part where I was and this is where we used to wash our hands, and to the right was a bathroom where people took baths.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There was also a door shown on the far side of that room, not where you showed us you entered, but on the other side of that room. Was that door kept open or closed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those, that door from our side was closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, if I could ask you to point out for the court where you were and where Dule Tadic was on the first occasion when you saw him in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot reach.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You can walk around. You can use the pointer and perhaps you can walk around as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here. (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you see those yellow markers to your left on the witness table? Can you take the one marked "W1" and place it where you were on that first occasion, and can you take the one marked "T1" and place it where Dule Tadic was on that first occasion? Mr. Haskic, can you point out where you were, where you were sitting on the second occasion when you saw Dule Tadic and where Dule Tadic was on that second occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was here and he was approximately here at the same spot, and I was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you take the marker marked "W2" and "T2"? As long as you are up there now, I know you referred to a third occasion, can you show us where you were on that third occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was here towards the end, towards the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you take the marker marked "W3", and can you take the marker marked "T3" and show us where the group you saw on that third occasion was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was all mostly in one area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If you could resume your seat, please? Mr. Haskic, I would like to direct your attention once more to the second occasion when you saw Dule Tadic in Omarska. You have already shown us where you were sitting and you have told us in what direction you were facing. Approximately how long after the first time you had seen Dule Tadic was it when you saw him for a second time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a very short period of time, perhaps a day or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On the second occasion was Dule Tadic alone or was he with others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was also a group of three to four people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How were the members of this group dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were Dule Tadic and the other members of the group doing when you saw them this second time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were standing and pointing something with their hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had anything drawn your attention to the area where Dule Tadic and the others were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, just the rumour that went through the inmates that this group with Dule arrived to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On this second occasion were you able to look long enough and enough times to make certain that it was Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how many times I could glance, but enough to see that it was him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mentioned that there was a third occasion and you have shown us on the model where you were at that time. Were you again sitting on the pista on that third occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what direction were you facing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also facing the canteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On this third occasion did you also hear that Dule Tadic was in camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you look to see if you could see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see him. I only saw him with his back turned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So on this third occasion, unlike the other two, although you heard he was in camp, you were not able to actually see his face on this occasion and make sure it was him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The group that you saw who had their backs turned to you, what were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you recall about how long after the second time you saw Dule Tadic in camp it was that you saw this group which had its back turned to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a very brief period of time, also perhaps a day or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Haskic, I realise there is a lot of equipment here in the courtroom but I would ask you to look carefully around the courtroom and tell us if you see Dule Tadic here in the courtroom? Can you look around, please, and tell us if Dule Tadic is here today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TADIC
utterances.text: Ya sam Dusko Tadic. (The accused Tadic rose to his feet and identified himself as Dusko Tadic).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise that man as being Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Are you absolutely sure that this is the man you saw on two occasions on the pista in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The record will reflect that the witness identified the accused. Mr. Wladimiroff and Mr. Tieger, I think that we need to talk with you at a recess regarding this matter. Cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Haskic, I first of all want to ask you some questions about how well you knew Dusko Tadic. First of all, have you ever lived in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in Kozarac. I lived in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In 1992 you were living in Prijedor, how long had you lived in Prijedor for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived in Prijedor from 1980.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The restaurant that you had, the Banja Luka Grill, where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was in the old market.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your businesses, were they in Prijedor as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say that you knew Dusko Tadic, would I be right in saying that you did not see him regularly when you were in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How Dusko Tadic spent his time when you were living in Prijedor you would be unable to help this court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Any periods that Dusko Tadic may have lived away from the Kozarac region, you would be unable to help this court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told the court this morning that you were part of a group of people who left a house that was not your own as a result of a command from military forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The house that you were in at that time was a building owned by a friend of yours?
