utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was he a relative?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But a number of other people like you had taken refuge where he lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It would be right to say, would it not, that when you were taken into custody on that day by those people that that changed your life?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they locked us up in the camp, yes, that changed my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: From that day onwards, the time that you had previously spent building up your businesses, providing your home in Prijedor, was something that you had lost for ever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lost it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Those events that occurred to you meant that you had to start a new life elsewhere and there has been no opportunity for you to go back to your home and resume your previous existence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not possible even today to go back to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Presumably, the people who did that to you, you feel a great deal of animosity towards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you have feelings of hatred to those people who on that day caused your life to be altered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot judge about those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You know that Dusko Tadic has been charged with the murder of your wife's brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have given a number of interviews, is that right, to the media concerning those events that took place in the summer of 1992 that you experienced?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not give, I only gave one interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You did not give more than one interview, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Very well. Do you recollect that in July 1994 you were interviewed by people in Germany through an interpreter who questioned you about events in Prijedor as well as Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you to look here at a document that is in German but signed by you upon each page. Your Honour, for record purposes, that would be, as I understand we are moving up the scale now, I think D18. Mr. Haskic, if you would like to just look at that document that I have put before you and you can see that it has typing on the front, but it also contains your signature at the foot of the page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that right? Do you remember ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- being questioned in Germany about what had happened in Prijedor and Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think on that occasion there was a police inspector present or chief criminal investigator, do you remember? Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And an interpreter who read back to you in your own language what you had told the chief criminal investigator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That interpreter was an Albanian, an Albanian in Albanian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the interpreter not speak to you in Serbo-Croatian and you acknowledged that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. I would just like you to turn to page 37 of that statement. They are numbered in the top right-hand corner. You can see your signature is on that page along with those of other people; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you, in fact, speak German?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You see, what I am going to suggest to you now is that on that occasion, on 5th July 1994, you gave a different story as to what had happened to you in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told this court here what happened to me, the same statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you not say on that occasion that the Serbs reached your house at 3 o'clock in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That could have been only a mistake in translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That the Serbs rang the bell and "I opened the door"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the Serbs only shot with their weapons. I was not in the house at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: "... that the Serbs demanded that I came out into the street", did you say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is very different, is it not, from what you have told this court today about what happened to you on that day that Muslims in Prijedor were rounded up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Today I said exactly what happened in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you told the court this morning about moving down your own street and there you saw your house on fire, did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see Fuad Ekimovic being shot or did you just see his body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As we were walking, I heard firing and we were passing by the house. I saw him lying dead by the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You see, did you tell people in Germany on this occasion: "There I could see a Serbian soldier shoot my neighbour, Fuad Ekimovic, in the head"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them shoot -- I heard a shot, and I saw him dead in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you go on to say that, in fact, about 50 people from your street were taken to a tower block where buses were waiting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were loaded on to buses. There were very many people. About 50 people would be loaded on to one bus and I knew various people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You see, what I am suggesting is that you have made up stories of things that you say that you have seen out of revenge for what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not invent it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say you saw Dusko Tadic two or three times in Omarska, that those sightings have been made up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not invent it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just looking at the first time you say you saw Mr. Tadic, how many people were with you on the pista at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not say exactly. I could not say the number of people who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you gave the statement in Germany you said there were about 1,000 other prisoners on the asphalt area in the camp, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were many.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would you agree or disagree with that figure of 1,000?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On the pista at that time, was that where you spent both the day and night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After the short stay in the restaurant building when you were first taken to Omarska, that was the place where you were in for quite a few days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I arrived at Omarska I spent one day in the room next to the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You then spent, are you able to tell us how many days, on the pista for day and night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the pista I spent 10 days as the maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This was at a time when the weather was very hot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The sun was beating down on the pista and you had no shade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had shade from the hangar only in the morning hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The rest of the day you were under the sun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The area of the pista was full of men like you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not all of the pista was filled up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The camp was very crowded at that time, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were very many people in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know or was any reason given to you that you had to stay out there because there was no room to put you anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The pista?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were on the pista because there was no room elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were on the pista were you free to roam about, to walk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The rest of the time you had to sit with your head between your legs looking at the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, or to lie down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you given access to the canteen at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was no canteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How were you fed when you were on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Like other prisoners, one eighth of a loaf of bread and a few spoons full of something of some liquid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On the pista did you eat that outside or did you go into the main restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went to a building, to the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: While you were on the pista were there any sanitary arrangements for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not on the pista. There were inside, in the building next to the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The first time you say that you saw Dusko Tadic there, there would have been a large number of people between you and the man that you say you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were very many behind me and to the side of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Looking at the place where you marked the model this morning, you put yourself in an area not very far away from the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Closer, nearer to the hangar than to the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Quite a substantial degree closer to the hangar than the restaurant, would you not agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not really say how closer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Somehow you say that on that day more people were behind you and to the side than sitting in the other area of the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were in a specific part of the pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That area of the pista, was it marked by anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was concrete, something like concrete, concrete something, like concrete vases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In a box shape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes square shaped. There was soil in them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The sort of thing that in better times maybe had flowers in them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They were between the edge of the restaurant building up to the hangar on both side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Those objects were on both sides of the building of the hangar to where we were, on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that the area that you were within bounded by the concrete tubs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were individual boxes. They did not run the length of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But looking at where you placed yourself this morning as having been sitting on that first occasion when you say you saw Dusko Tadic, would you not agree with me that there would have been many people between you and that figure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were many people on the pista, and ahead of me there were not many people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On the second occasion you are again closer to the hangar than the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Closer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And that is where you marked those positions this morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, were there not many people between you and the person you say was Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time there were more since I was nearer to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As you told the Court this morning, on that first time you just cast a glance so as not to be noticed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There were dangers for you in looking up and around because guards did not permit that, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again on that second occasion all you could do was glance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To glance enough to see that it was he.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I suggest to you is that even if you did see someone in those kinds of circumstances, that in fact that was not Dusko Tadic that you said a person was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was a group of three or four persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you name on any of those three occasions that you saw him any of the other people who were with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The third time I only heard that Dvca had come with him but I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On any of those occasions could you name any of the people that you say he was with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you name any of the people who were sitting near you? Did you sit with the same group of people on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Different. It varied every day depending on who sat where.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember any of the people sitting with you on either of those occasions that you say you saw Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I cannot remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have described camouflage uniforms. Can you tell us anything about the appearance of the man you say you saw, a description?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he had a camouflage uniform. He was rather short and he was very well built.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you notice anything else about the appearance of the man, shaven or unshaven, beard or no beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You cannot picture it now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The length of the beard, I cannot determine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Length of hair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Haskic, you mentioned that the interpreter when you spoke with the German authorities was Albanian. Is there a difference in the way this interpreter spoke to you than the way a native speaker does?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A drastic difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At times did you have some difficulty understanding the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was it sometimes difficult to understand all the things the Albanian interpreter said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to look at page 35 in that statement? In the last paragraph there is a reference to what happened in Prijedor and it says it was a "Nacht und Nebel" attack. Do you what "Nacht und Nebel" is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I step forward to the model just for a moment? It is difficult for me to see from here.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Haskic, was the entire pista area from the back of the hangar to the doorstep of the restaurant building occupied by prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there room in front of the restaurant building for ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that for guards to walk into, for prisoners to go to get their meals and so on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and so that the guards can move.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the portion of the pista which the prisoners occupied was set back from the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was. There was some empty space.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now you tried to put that rather big yellow marker in the approximate area where you were on the first occasion when you saw Dule Tadic in Omarska, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall on that first occasion, however, that you were closer to the front of the group of prisoners in the section of the pista that the prisoners sat, and there were more prisoners behind you than in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Haskic, during the years that you were familiar with Dule Tadic did you know him to have a heavy growth of beard or hair on his face? Was his hair dark and did it grow quickly on his face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a black beard and, yes, he had a very strong beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If he did not shave for a few days did he already have the appearance of a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think the witness said he had a black beard rather than not shaving for a few days. I think my learned friend has taken a step, your Honour, that is not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will overrule your objection. You can enquire in cross-examination. He just asked if he had not shaved for a few days would he have a beard. You can question him on cross-examination about what he said when you spoke to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Haskic, I asked you a few moments ago whether Mr. Tadic's hair was dark and whether it grew quickly on his face. You said he had a black beard and he had a very strong beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: By that did you mean that he was the kind of person whose hair grew quickly and which showed up on his face quickly if he did not shave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Haskic, did you contact the German authorities to speak with them or did they contact you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did. They called me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they tell you they understood you had been in Omarska camp and that you might have information about what happened in camp and what happened in Prijedor generally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know whether they knew before that, but they knew I had been to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you go to see the German authorities for the purpose of speaking to them about the attack on Prijedor and your experiences in camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About the attack on Prijedor and about the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the course of that discussion did they ask you about Dule Tadic? Did you receive any interpretation sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not remember. I could not say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you tell the German authorities when you spoke to them that you had seen Dule Tadic on the pista in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, are you telling the court the truth this day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would you invent any portion of your ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just one matter, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Haskic, can you confirm this, that the statement you gave in Germany on 5th July 1994 was made in relation to proceedings against Mr. Tadic that were within the German Criminal Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, perhaps I can do it through you. If you could find out from the witness whether he can give any date at all as to his first sighting on the pista of Tadic, because I do not think that has emerged, has it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, my recollection of the testimony is this, that the witness arrived in Omarska on the evening of May 30th, as he testified. I believe he said he spent one night in the restaurant building, was taken to the pista. Perhaps you are right, perhaps the question in between ----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: There is a stay in the White House and then there are 10 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I will clarify that. I understand the point. Mr. Haskic, do you recall approximately how long after you were placed on the pista it was before you saw Dule Tadic for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not say. The first time I saw him, the first time, between the first time and the second time, a day or two elapsed, but as to the first time I could not really say whether it was a day or two or ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were on the pista for a total of approximately 10 days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not more than 10 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it during that time that you spent one night in the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have no questions. Is there any objection to Mr. Haskic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we may require this witness's further attendance and I would ask that he not be released on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Not? You do not mean today but just be subject to ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A further recall, if appropriate.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I will leave that to the court, your Honour. There is certainly no reason on the Prosecution's part why this witness cannot be excused.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Haskic, Counsel for the Defence has asked that you be available so that, if necessary, you can be recalled to testify before the Trial Chamber. So, please make sure that you keep in touch with the Office of the Prosecutor who has called you as a witness, and they know where you are, so that, if necessary, you can be recalled. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Will you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. We will stand in recess until 2.30.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you like to call your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. We call Saud Hrnic. MR. SAUD HRNIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take that oath that is before you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, would you please state your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Saud Hrnic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: April 4th, in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is the year of your birth?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you born in the town of Kozarac or in one of the villages surrounding the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the town of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you live in the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived there until the 24th -- 27th May 1994.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you attend primary school in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you attend secondary school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you serve in the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did you serve in the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between January 1980 to 1981.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were your duties in the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the motorized unit, I transported people, equipment, food stuffs and the rest.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You were a driver?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As a result of your service in the military, did you become familiar with JNA equipment, uniforms and weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, most of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you become familiar with JNA vehicles and combat vehicles such as tanks or amoured personnel carriers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your former occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question -- before the army or after it?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Before the attack on Kozarac, what was your former occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had my own private delivery, own shipping company.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That was some type of trucking company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did your trucking company take you into the villages in the areas surrounding Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As a result of your business did you meet and know many of the people in the villages surrounding Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the predominant ethnic group or groups in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were there some Serb villages and areas as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have any business other than this trucking company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From '91, in mid '91, I had a discotheque in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was that discotheque located in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards the bus station, at the bus station in Kozarac, in the Local Commune.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you live in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Marsala Tita Street, 140.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If the witness could be provided with Prosecution Exhibit 196, the map of a portion of Kozarac? Sir, if you could take a moment to examine that map? If the map could then be put on the overhead projector, please? Sir, if we are looking at this map and we see the main street running by the school and toward the building marked "mosque", that being the main street of Kozarac, could you please point out to the court where your home would have been located? Please do that on the overhead projector exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the map).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So your home would have been just beyond the mosque that is located on that map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That is the Mutnik mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many homes away from the mosque would your home have been located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five or six from the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Looking at this same map could you show us approximately where your disco would have been located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here at the crossroads, here on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So it would have been on the opposite side of the street from the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Yes, yes, but before the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: But on the other side of Marsala Tita?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, Kozarac was a fairly small town, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did your business and other activities take you often into the main area of town along this main street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know many of the inhabitants of the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know many of the people and businesses located along Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long have you known Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, about when I started elementary school and then onward, later around my 10th.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Around your 10th what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, the translation said "around my 10th", around your 10th what, your 10th birthday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, is Dule Tadic younger than you or older than you are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Older.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, he is approximately how much older than you are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five or six years.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you first become aware of Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As a child, I admired his brothers and later I watched him. They were outstanding karateists and I liked it as a child, I liked to watch them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you would occasionally watch them as they trained at karate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever take karate lessons from Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many courses of karate training did you take from Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I attended his course twice.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How old were you when you first attended his course?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, somewhere around 16 or 17.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did this first course last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It lasted longer than that, but I spent two or three months there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many times a week would you be in training with Dule Tadic in this course?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once or twice.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Once or twice what, a week, a month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A week.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This second course that you took from Dule Tadic, how long did this course last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly, but briefly.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You attended this course only briefly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not say exactly how long it lasted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you complete this course or did you leave this course before it was completed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why did you leave it before it was completed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had an opportunity to spar with a friend of mine, and during that dual I hit him with my foot unintentionally and he fell on the floor; and then Dule Tadic came up and began beating me because of that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After this second course and after you left this second course, did you continue to have contact with Dule Tadic after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of contact would you have with Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we met in the street or at a cafe bar.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did your sister have a cafe bar in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the name of that cafe bar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was cafe bar Trinaest, 13.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you ever in that cafe bar when Dule Tadic was also in that cafe bar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was Dule Tadic's business in Kozarac, what was his occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the eve of the war he also started a cafe bar, and before that he was an active athlete and long before that he had coached people and so on.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: His cafe bar was located where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was next to his family's house, his father's house and his.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That was located where in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was to the left slightly before the school or the restaurant, to the left, facing down Kozarac from the direction of the Banja Luka/Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This was on Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever have occasion to go to Dule Tadic's cafe bar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time that you knew Dule Tadic, on a weekly basis how frequently would you say you had contact with Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Although he had his own cafe bar, he frequently visited the cafe bar of my sister and my brother-in-law and we met there rather often and in his cafe pub too.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On a weekly basis how often would you say you would have contact with Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, let me say I did not have much contact with him, but we met in the street. We simply come across each other in the street.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would this occur frequently during a week, occasionally -- how frequently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not know the exact number, but very often.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know Dule Tadic's wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know if she worked and, if so, do you know what her occupation was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she was a nurse or something else, I would not know exactly, but she was employed in the hospital. For a certain period of time she was in the Kozarac hospital.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time that you knew Dule Tadic did you ever see Dule Tadic with a fully grown beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were there periods of time when you saw Dule Tadic and he would be clean shaven?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but very seldom. One could not see whether he was clean shaven or not unless you came very close up to him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule Tadic had quite a strong beard, and if you look at him from a certain distance one could think that he had a beard when he did not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So he had a strong, dark facial hair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time that you knew Dule Tadic how would you characterise your relationship with him? Would you say you were acquaintances, friends or good friends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I would rather say we knew each other from the street. We were no close friends, but when we would meet we sometimes spend sometime together in company together, but we did not have much contact.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was there anyone in the Kozarac area who looked very similar to Dusko Tadic in appearance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever hear other people talking about a person that they had mistaken for Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know of any of Dule Tadic's close friends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who were some of his very close friends, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think his closest friend was Emir Karabasic who often spent days with him and even nights often.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know Emir Karabasic's ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time I would ask that Prosecution Exhibit 195 be played? This is a video of portions of Kozarac, just the Marsala Tita Street portion, please? Mr. Hrnic, as this is played, I would ask you to identify for the court structures that you recognise. Could you hold that for just a moment, please? I am sorry, your Honours, was there -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Our only concern is that we have seen Exhibit 195 several times. We could probably point out some places as well, but if you want to establish that this witness knew the area -----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: It is obvious he must do.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He had a disco place.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That is fine. If your Honours are satisfied with that, we will not show Prosecution Exhibit 195.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Unless there is some other reason for it?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour, there is not.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then please do not play that video. In the spring of 1992, you were living in Kozarac, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In the spring of 1992, do you recall ever seeing any cannon or artillery being moved into the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw this, what type of cannon or artillery did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, those were, one would say, light cannons. They were trailed by trucks and they were passing through Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise the light cannons as the type that the JNA had as weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise the trucks that were pulling them as JNA type trucks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see any type of licensed plates or markings on these trucks to identify them as JNA trucks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I saw the JNA plates, and they had -- and vehicles TAM 110. They were so-called Pitzgauers, they were TAM 110 or .....

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: A Pitzgauer was a military type vehicle used by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When was it that you saw these cannons being pulled by these JNA trucks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was in April or, perhaps, early May. I do not know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This was 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was it that you saw these cannons being pulled by these trucks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them entering the area of what we called the Vocnjak. It is Garevci, between two bus stations, Koncari and Orlovci.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see them being pulled along the new Prijedor/Banja Luka road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could have Prosecution Exhibit 79 provided to the witness? Sir, if you could take a moment and familiarise yourself with that map? If that map could be put on the overhead projector, please? Then if that area could be located, Mr. Hrnic? If you could point to the area in which you saw these vehicles? If you could point to the general area, we will then focus in on it more closely. If you could point to the Exhibit that is on the overhead projector?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is here. (The witness indicated on the map).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could come into that a little more closely, please? So it is near this area with the word just above it "Drljaca" that you saw these vehicles? Please point again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is not here -- yes, it is. Yes, Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw these vehicles pulling these cannon, in what direction were they moving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were coming from the direction of Banja Luka and they headed towards Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then did they leave the main highway and go in another direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please show the court where they left the main highway and the direction in which they went?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here, they moved towards above Vocnjak.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is in that area? There are green dots there. What is in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We called it Vocnjak. It is orchard. There were apple trees, plum trees, pear trees.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what ethnic group lives in and controls that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall if this was before or after the Serb takeover of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not know exactly, but I think it was before.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After 30th April Serb takeover in Prijedor, did you begin to have difficulties travelling between Kozarac and Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of difficulties did you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we came across points.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of points are you talking about, checkpoints on the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There were checkpoints of the police and the army, the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were these checkpoints located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first one was in Kozarac and the second one was in Koncari and the third one in Cirkin Polje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of difficulties did you have at these checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were all almost always stopped, checked, searched. Our cars were checked -- were searched.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that there were JNA and police at these checkpoints. What did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time the policemen were in their ordinary blue uniforms and the military were in many coloured camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of these people who manned these checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I knew most of them. There were traffic policemen, policemen who always were on the road between Prijedor and Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The ones that you knew, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Again after the Serb takeover of Prijedor, after this time, did the inhabitants of Kozarac organise any type of patrols or guard posts in the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of patrols or guard posts were organised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By and large, night guards in the streets and on the approaches to Kozarac, on those main exits roads to Kozarac, there were these checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why were these checkpoints, these guards posts, organised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly, they were afraid of somebody coming from the other side and create something that could turn into conflict.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say they were afraid of "people coming from the other side", who are you referring to by these "people coming from the other side"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: JNA army, and the people that could come, and I am not sure who they would be.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many people in Kozarac participated in these patrols or guard posts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you the exact number, but on the street there were always in the evening two people walking, and police were having their patrols.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The groups of people who would participate, what groups of people participated in these patrols?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Citizens, and Territorial Defence from Kozarac and police.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you one of these men who participated in these patrols?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What area did you patrol or guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was mostly in the area of Rajkovici and Mrakovica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where are those areas located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are located towards the direction -- when you go from Kozarac to Mrakovica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you look at Prosecution Exhibit 79, does that have Rajkovici on there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could that be placed back on the overhead, please, and then if you could show the court the area in which you would be involved in these patrols? If we could zoom in on that, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the map).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This was the road going up to where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That road that goes through Mrakovica towards Bosanska Gradiska.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was this also the road that you would take if you went to Mount Kozara?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The groups of people involved in these patrols, was there any type of formal chain of command, a military type chain of command, for these groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In these groups would there be a person who was usually in charge of the group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many of these people were armed, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Usually, policemen were armed and policemen who were at those checkpoints and the people who had their own weapons, but there were very few of those.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You also mentioned that there were persons who were members of the Territorial Defence who participated in these patrols. Would some of those individuals also have weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of weapons did the people have who participated in these patrols?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly hunting rifles and some people had M48 rifles which came from TO, and I think there was maybe a machine gun that belonged to TO.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were there any automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were some automatic weapons but very few.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of weapon did you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had an automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How much ammunition did the people have for these weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very little.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did these people have any mortars or cannons or artillery weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did these people have any tanks or amoured personnel carriers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know or know of a person by the name of Cirkin who was called Captain Cirkin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know him personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did he have any involvement in organising these groups of people who patrolled Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like for you again to use Prosecution Exhibit 79 and, using that map, I would like you to show the court where you were on 24th May 1992 when the attack on Kozarac began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was above Rajkovici, on the road to Kotlovaca, here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So this was in the area near the word "Alagic" on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know this word.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You see the word on the map and you have pointed to an area close to that word?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see, I see. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This was one of these checkpoints that you had mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why did you have a checkpoint in that particular area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this was sort of the end of the town of Kozarac, and it was on the main road that took from Rajkovici to Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were there any JNA installations further up that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was that installation or installations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were soldiers, JNA soldiers, perhaps some members of the reserve units, but they were within JNA.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where they were located, the name of that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On 24th April (sic), when the attack began, where was your family? Where was your wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were at home.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you have children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were your children at home with your wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I misspoke. I said 24th April when the attack began; I meant 24th May. I apologise. So on 24th May, your wife was at home, your children were not at home in Kozarac. Where were your children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They went abroad.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When the attack began on Kozarac and you became aware of the attack, did you remain where you were or did you leave the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I left the area.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you leave the area on foot or in a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you left the area did you drive through the main street of Kozarac and out of the town in the direction of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were driving through the main street of Kozarac and out of the town, was that area being shelled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time did you hear any shelling, any firing, coming from the town outward toward Serbs positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At some point did you yourself come under direct fire from a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could, again using Prosecution Exhibit 79, point to your location when you came under direct fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the map).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is that area that you have pointed to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is called Forica Suma.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could point there again, please? I would note that it is to the left of the word "Nisici". Were you able to determine the location from which this fire was coming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was this fire coming from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was coming from above Drenovici, from the bridge over Balte.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could point to that area, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the map).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How far away would that area have been from where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think about two to three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was that area you pointed out at a higher elevation than you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what ethnic group controlled that area from which the firing was coming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you able to determine what type of weaponry was being fired at you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were mortars.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you able to escape from this small wood and move to another area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you able to escape from this area where you were under fire and move to another location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you remain out of the town of Kozarac then until Monday afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On Monday, before you returned to the area of Kozarac, did you see any tanks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you see the tanks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the same place, in Balte.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many tanks did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw one.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you able to determine if the tank was firing at the time you saw it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you able to determine that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was quite close, I am not sure at what distance, but several kilometres and I could see how the tank was turned towards the city and I could see the smoke coming out.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you also hear anything being fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In what direction was the tank pointed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pointed towards Kamicani, Softici, that direction.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was the ethnic group of the people who lived in those areas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you returned to the town of Kozarac on Monday, did you spend the night in a cellar of a house there in the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The next morning then, on Tuesday, did you see people beginning to surrender and move toward the main business area of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you when these people were beginning to form a column and move toward the centre business area of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was close to the police station before, in front of the PTT and cafe Neira.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw these people in this column moving toward the centre of Kozarac, did you recognise any of those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any policemen among those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who were the policemen that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were Osme, Police Commander, Braco Denic, and other policemen.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These policemen that you recognised, to your knowledge, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw them, when you saw the police, where were they in this group of people? Were they toward the front or were they in the middle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards the front.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could use Prosecution Exhibit 196 again, please, the map of portions of Kozarac, and if you could please point to the area where you saw this group of people including these police.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the map).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So this would be an area just below the circular road that branched off from Marsala Tita and then rejoined it at a lower place on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That road does not join lower on the map; it joins on the upper part of the map.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes. If would you point again, please? So the area that you saw them is below the road as it joins Marsala Tita, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Below the road where it joins.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw this group of people there, did you see any escorts or soldiers with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At the time that you saw this group of people, could you estimate how many people were in this group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a huge number of people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On this same map further up, there is a structure that is indicated as a motel. It has earlier been identified as a structure that was set up as a temporary hospital and police headquarters. After you saw Osme and Braco, at some time after that, did you make your way to this motel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you arrived at this motel who did you see there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw policemen at the motel and some civilians but very few.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these policemen at the motel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, most of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The ones that you recognised, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of any of these policemen that you saw at the motel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were those names that you recall, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nedjo Redzic, Emir Hodzic, Ekrem Besic, Besic -- I forgot his first name, we called him "Boca" -- Klipic, Sakip, and many others.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You mentioned the name Klipic, did you know Klipic's first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we all of us called him "Klipic".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, what was his wife's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Nasiha.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you arrived at the motel and you saw these policemen, what were the policemen doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all there and they tried to establish connection with Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was trying to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Edin Besic, we called him Boca, tried to do that. He tried to get a connection with the police station in Prijedor, I think, with the station, police station Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, who was he trying to reach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was asking to talk to Osme on the telephone.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To the Commander of police in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did he ever make contact with Osme over the radio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At some point after you arrived at the motel, did this group of policemen leave the motel and head in a direction toward the business centre of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After you saw them going in that direction, did you see any of them again after that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you yourself surrender on that date, on Tuesday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you able to reunite with your wife late that night on Tuesday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The next day, the Wednesday, did you and your wife join with other people who were going toward the centre of Kozarac to surrender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time were you walking or were you in a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Walking.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time did you have any weapons with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What had you done with the weapon which you had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On Tuesday morning when the first group wanted to surrender, when they went to surrender, we left at a friend's -- we put it in a friend's bag.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did this group, including yourself and your wife, ultimately stop near the school on Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the bus station in Kozarac, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As you walked toward this area, did you see any people with weapons standing up on any of the buildings in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of clothing were these people wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They all had camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of weapons did they have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had mostly automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As you went on this route toward the centre of town did you see any tanks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After I got to that spot, I could see a tank that was standing at the junction where the road that goes to the old Kula is, and the road that goes to Stari Grad, the old town.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So this was a junction of Marsala Tita and another street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The tank that you saw, did you recognise it as a JNA type tank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As you made your way to this area in Kozarac did you have any armed escorts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these escorts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were these escorts wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They all wore camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When this column finally came to a halt, using Prosecution Exhibit 196, could you show the court where this column of people was finally halted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the map) Here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You are pointing here at the intersection with what is called sometimes the old Prijedor road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you kept at that intersection before you moved on from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you exactly -- perhaps two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were being held there, did you have any police or soldiers who were guarding you or escorting you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know his name, but we called him Gauro's son.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These guards that you had at this intersection, what were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They all had camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were waiting at this intersection area, did you see any looting going on in structures near you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw the truck in front of Redzo's house, that is, my friend's house, a truck had Bosanski Novi plate, it was a civilian truck, and it was loading on -- the people were loading everything from the store on to the truck.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said that this was the store of a friend of yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was this friend's ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were these looters wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While these people in camouflage uniforms were looting this store, did the guards with you intervene to stop them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were the guards doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They tried to see what is there in the store, what could they take for them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at this intersection, was this large group separated into smaller groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you separated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Men were separated from women.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After you were separated in what direction did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went towards the new road Banja Luka/Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then in what direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As you initially set out were you in vehicles or were you on foot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On foot, we walked.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were the men and the women and children eventually put on to buses and then taken to Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
