utterances.text: The women were first put on the buses and children, and they were taken away.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then the men were put on buses and taken to Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this might be a good time to break.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may be seated, please. Miss Hollis, would you like to continue?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Sir, I would like to clarify two matters before we continue with the questioning. I had asked you earlier if you knew the ethnic group of Emir Karabasic and I do not recall what your answer was. Could you tell us, please, if you know, what was the ethnic group of Emir Karabasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We had also talked earlier about the Monday after the attack on Kozarac, and that you had seen a tank in Balte. You had testified earlier that Balte was an area inhabited by Serbs. You had also indicated that the turret of the tank was pointed toward the area of Kamicani and Softici. Could you tell us, please, the ethnic group of the people who lived in the Kamicani and Softici area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. At the break you had indicated that the men, women and children had been put on to buses on the Wednesday after the attack on Kozarac. You yourself were also put on one of these buses, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of buses were these that were used to transport these groups of people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were civilian buses of Auto Transport in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you arrive at Trnopolje camp on Wednesday, the Wednesday following the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At Trnopolje camp were you reunited with your wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you remain at Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About five days.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did your wife remain at Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two days.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the date that you were taken from Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was 1st June.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you able to keep track of dates after you were taken by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I paid no attention to dates, but I am speaking approximately. My wife left on Friday, I know that, and I left two days later.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your recollection is that two days after that Friday was 1st June, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was 1st, that it was 1st June.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Trnopolje camp, where did you sleep in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the school.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of the other people being detained at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, most of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of the people you knew being detained at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did the camp guards wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all in camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of these camp guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The ones that you knew, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Trnopolje camp do you recall seeing a woman shot and killed there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see of this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were outside at the corner of the school, well, in the yard practically and we were paying no attention, but there was a fire and then we turned and saw a soldier raise his automatic rifle and start firing at people who were outside.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see this woman hit by that fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you left Trnopolje camp, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The barracks in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That was the military barracks in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, where are those military barracks located in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where are they located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the exit from Prijedor, in the direction of Bosanska Dubica, on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Are there any other towns in that general direction as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this is the road to Zagreb, to Belgrade/Zagreb highway, and quite a number of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held at the military barracks in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Enough to write a statement.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you transported to the military barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were transferred with Fadil Delmic and his car.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who drove that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two soldiers seized his car and put him and me in the car and drove it, and then on the way I realised we were heading for the barracks and we did arrive at the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said that you were in the barracks long enough to give a statement. You were questioned while you were at the barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who questioned you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two uniformed individuals. I saw their ranks but I do not know them, in many coloured camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the statement about? What did they ask you about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They wanted me to write where I was at the beginning of the war, what I did before the war and what I did during the attack on Kozarac until my stay in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you taken after you gave that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took me to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you transported to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who escorted you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were again two soldiers but other two soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms too.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seven days.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were there where were you held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in a garage No. 1.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time if Prosecution Exhibit 201 could be provided and that would be document No. 29-1, 29/27, if that could be brought up on the computer screen? Mr. Hrnic, do you recognise this photograph as a photograph of Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that could be placed on the overhead projector, please? Sir, if you could please point to the location where you were held in Keraterm pointing to the photograph that is on the overhead projector?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you point there again, please? So this is the first set of doors to the left as you view this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That was garage No. 1 in which you were kept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Keraterm, did you know or recognise any of the other detainees being held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The detainees that you knew or recognised, to your knowledge, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of them were Muslims and there were a couple of Croats.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you personally know any of the guards at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The person that you knew, what was that person's ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The guards at Keraterm wore what type of clothing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They also wore camouflage uniforms, by and large, camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: "By and large", what other types of clothing did you see the guards there wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, sometimes somebody would turn up, I do not know, police, for instance, police uniforms. There were old SMB uniforms, the old uniforms, those of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Keraterm did you learn of a man who was called Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did others at Keraterm point out this man to you as Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I did not know his name but I did see him before that on various occasions.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Other individuals told you his name was Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That he was Zigic, a few people called him Zoran, but I knew him. I had seen him on a number of occasions before that. I did not know his name.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Keraterm, do you recall any occasions when detainees were beaten at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who did the beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoran Zigic was the one who beat the most.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall an occasion when you saw Zoran Zigic beat a man named Emsud Bahonic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see this beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How was this man, Emsud Bahonic, beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was beaten, Zigic beat him. He had a scorpion with him, he always had it with him. A scorpion is a pistol. He kicked him with his feet, with anything that he happened to come by. There were also some rods there -- whatever he could lay his hands on.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see Emsud Bahonic's condition after this beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember whether it was the left or the right side, but he could not move one side of his body at all.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see any other bruising or injuries on his body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was bruised all over.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Had you known Emsud Bahonic before Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of Emsud Bahonic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you left Keraterm where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took me to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you taken there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took us in a police van.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have escorts in that police van?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say. We were locked up in the van. There were 12 or 13 of us. We were inside. I could not see anything. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These other individuals who were taken with you, were these other detainees from Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the date when you arrived at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was 8th June.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the day of the week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could have been Monday possibly or perhaps Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held at Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there until August 6th 1992 or 7th.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you left Omarska where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took us to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you personally know any of the guards at Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Of the guards that you knew what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did the guards at Omarska camp wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in many coloured uniforms, in uniforms as the police were, then also old SMB uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Omarska camp, did you ever meet or see a man named Zeljko Mejakic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at the camp did you learn what his position was in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was his position in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Commander of the camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why do you believe he was the Commander of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was there almost every day, every night. He rarely left the camp. He did not communicate with the detainees much, only with the guards and the superiors.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of the other detainees at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, many of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The detainees that you knew, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim, mostly.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have any relatives at Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What relatives did you have at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, first, there was my brother, Hrnic Dalija, there was another relative of mine, Jasmin Hrnic; there was one of my brothers-in-law, a number of my friends and brother of one of my brothers-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that Jasmin Hrnic was a relative of yours. Did Jasmin Hrnic have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what was that nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Jasko".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your relatives who were at the camp, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you would, please, look at this model in front of you and if you could tell us what the large red building is almost directly in front of you, what building was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is hangar.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The area between the hangar and the smaller red building, what was that area called?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is pista.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The smaller red building that is somewhat to your right, what building was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was the administrative building and the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Can you see the smaller white building on the model?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was the white house.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As you look at this model before you, was this the setup of Omarska camp as it was when you were there in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you first arrived at Omarska, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They brought us there, here, took us out, and lined us up against the wall of this building.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I noticed that you initially pointed to an area in the pista and then you pointed to an area near what you have identified as the administration or restaurant building. Sir, if I could ask you for the moment if you would refrain from pointing and later I will ask you to point to some positions. Sir, once you were lined up what was done, what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were ordered to take out everything from our pockets or whatever we had, and we also had some bags in Keraterm. We were carrying around underwear and things like that. They all took it away from us and then they took us towards the hangar. When they took us there, I did not know it was called the white house, but on the other side they took us to the door to the first floor and to the first room to the right, and we learnt later on that it was called 15.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So they took you into the hangar up on to the first floor and they put you in the first room on the right at the top of the stairs, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That was room No. 15, you learned later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you first arrived at Omarska, as you were being searched and as you were being moved to this room 15, were you beaten or otherwise abused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that day.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you first arrived at Omarska did you see other detainees -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I cannot hear very well.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry. When you first arrived at Omarska did you see other detainees at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were these other detainees, what general area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first I saw were on the pista.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw them on the pista, what was their position, their body was positioned how on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all lying down prone.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to ask you a few questions about conditions at Omarska camp while you were there. While you were there, how many times a day were you fed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once or no times at all.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were fed what type of food did you receive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, water. I do not know really what to call it, it was not soup, no spices, nothing, almost without salt.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How much time were you given to eat this one meal a day that you sometimes received?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we knew it was three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you have this one meal a day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the administrative building where the restaurant is.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What would happen if you took more than three minutes for a meal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I, well, you really do not feel very hungry if I told you about that; we were beaten.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you given water to drink while you were at the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very seldom.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This water that you were given to drink, what was the quality of this water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was perhaps from the River Gomenica; it must have been industrial effluence, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there a particular taste or smell to this water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was dirty. It was running through those large pipes that are used to wash their trucks, those dumper trucks, or other vehicles they had there in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have indicated that you were held in Omarska from early June until 6th August; what were the temperatures like during the time you were held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That year the heat was unbearable.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were the hygienic conditions like when you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had a bath practically on the eve of my departure to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were there adequate toilets or other facilities for the people at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were first taken to the camps, do you know what your weight was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, about 100 kilogrammes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Omarska or later at Manjaca were you ever weighed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was that that you were weighed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was the Rote Kreuz, or whatever it was called, when they arrived first, I would not know the date, but they were the ones who weighed us.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So this was the Red Cross that weighed you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time how much weight had you lost?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 32 kilogrammes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said that when you first arrived you were taken to room 15 in the hangar building. Could you tell us how long you were held in room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: About how long were you in the camp before you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some 12 days or so, 10, 12 days. I know the day when I was interrogated for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this point if we can please unplug the overhead projector and plug in the camera for the model? If we can also have the roof taken off, the lower roof, on the hangar building? Sir, at this time I am going to ask you to move around to the side or the front of the model and point to the room in which you were held, the room which was called room 15. Before you do that, let me also ask that when you look into that room you are going to see a number or some numbers on a piece of paper in the room and I am going to ask you to tell us what that number is. You may want to take off your headphones as you move around and then you can put on headphones that are near the Registrar's table. So if you would take off your headphones now, please, and take the pointer and move around so that you can see room 15? Sir, if you could come to my side of the model towards me, can you see room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could one of the microphones be turned towards the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you please point with the pointer to room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model)

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would note that he is pointing to the large room that has B7. It appears to be B23. Sir, while you are looking at that, could you please point to the door through which you were brought into that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could point to the inside of that door in the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Then if you could please resume your seat? The technician may wish to resume his seat at this time. Sir, while you were held in room 15, do you have any idea of how many people were also held in this room with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In your estimation, how many people were held in that room with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time while I was there about 300 people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of these other people being held in room 15 with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The people that you knew, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have indicated that you believe you were interrogated perhaps 10 or 12 days after you were taken to the camp. During the first week at the camp were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you speak in terms of weeks, do you speak in terms of a week as Monday to the next Monday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So, for that first week until the next Monday you were not interrogated, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then the second week that you were there, during the week itself, prior to the weekend, were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Saturday.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So, Monday through Friday you were not interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then Saturday was the first time you were taken for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was the second week, not the first week.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right. Prior to that interrogation, that first time you were taken for interrogation on a Saturday, do you recall an incident involving a man named Meho Alic during which incident Meho Alic was called out of room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you observe happen during this incident involving Meho Alic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Meho -- a guard came in that I did not know from before. He opened the door and he called out "Meho Alic". He got up, and then he asked for Meho Alic to go out and find his son.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So the guard came to the door; was this the same door that you showed us earlier into room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So he came to that door and he called "Meho Alic" and then Meho Alic stood up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then he asked Meho Alic something about his son?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did he ask Meho Alic to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked, he wanted Meho to go and find his son Eno.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After he told Meho that is what he wanted, did Meho then leave room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On this occasion when Meho was called out of room 15, do you recall if any other men in that room were also called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Emir Beganovic and Senad Muslimovic left the room.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of these three men before this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many of these men did you know before the incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew Meho, Began, and naturally Senad who was Halid Muslimovic's brother.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While Meho was gone from the room, what did you hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is hard to say. We heard what we would rather not have heard. There was sounds of breaking, screams. There was one scream that I particularly remember it. I still have goose bumps when I remember it now. I cannot even describe this.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did Meho Alic eventually come back to the room, room 15, that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When he came back to the room what was his behaviour or demeanour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me tell you, he could not even walk. He was pale. He came back and sat down. Nobody even asked him anything.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your recollection, what time of the day was it that Meho Alic was called from the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your recollection, how many days before your first interrogation did this incident occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two days.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that Meho Alic was asked to leave the room and find his son Eno. Did you know his son Eno?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know Eno by any other name other than Eno?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We all called him either "Alic" which was his last name, Eno Alic, and we all knew him under that last name. "Eno" is short for his full first name.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When Meho was called out, were you in the area of room 15 that was closest to the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was Meho Alic also in that area of the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The guard who called out to Meho Alic, did you recognise this guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was this guard wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He also had camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have mentioned that your relative Jasmin or Jasko Hrnic was also in Omarska camp. Since this incident involving Meho Alic, have you ever seen your relative Jasmin Hrnic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have indicated that you believe you were first interrogated on a weekend a Saturday. In total, how many times were you taken for interrogation while you were at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five times.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In what building were those interrogations held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Administrative building.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During those five times you were taken for interrogation, were you interrogated in rooms both on the ground floor and the first floor of that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The times that you were taken for interrogation who would escort you for these interrogations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were certain young men and, apparently, each was working for a certain inspector.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of the people that escorted you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some had camouflage uniforms and some guards had police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The people who interrogated you, did you know any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only one.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was Laic -- Lakic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Lakic was from where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lakic was from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was Lakic's ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These other interrogators, do you know where they came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some were from Prijedor and some from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How do you know that they were from Prijedor or Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were in pista and I found this out while I was in pista. They would come in several cars from Banja Luka, and the bus was coming from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could see while we were on the pista, and through what we heard from the others who were there, but we could also see that. We could see the cars and the bus as they came.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was it about these cars and buses that made you know they were from Banja Luka or Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ones that came from Prijedor, they all had Banja Luka license plates and the bus belonged to Rudar, the football club Rudar, Ljubija and Omarska, they were all together in one group.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: My translation indicates that the ones that came from Prijedor all had Banja Luka license plates. Is that correct? The Prijedor vehicles had Banja Luka licensed plates?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I either did not understand or -- the cars had came from Prijedor. The bus had Prijedor license plates.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Those from Banja Luka had what kind of license plates?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no bus from Banja Luka there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The vehicles that came from Banja Luka had what kind of license plates?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the times that you were taken for interrogation were you beaten or otherwise abused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened to you? What type of abuse or beatings did you receive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time I was beaten on the ground floor, that was Monday, and that was during the second interrogation I was beaten unconscious. I managed to leave that room and go back to pista, until the next time. Then again I was called out by these people from Banja Luka. I went on the floor and I had to kneel there on a square that was maybe 50 by 50. Those were the squares like these ones in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You are pointing down to the squares of the carpeting on the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you were made to kneel on a square that was approximately what, 50 centimetres by 50 centimetres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were kneeling there what was done to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First, they warned us not to leave that square, and they would hit us from the back so that immediately you would have to leave the square. Then they would use their feet to put us back on the square. Then they would hit us with the sticks and whatever they had. There were three men there that beat me, and after that I did not even feel the blows. I did not care.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After this second beating where were you taken, back to room 15 or back to some other area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the second beating or the second interrogation?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The second interrogation, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took me back to pista.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that during your second interrogation, your first beating, you were beaten unconscious. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was unconscious. I was half conscious during the second interrogation and the first beating. That was Monday.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During any of these interrogations were you asked to sign anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of questions were you asked during the interrogations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most often they wanted to know my personal information. Then they asked about these people and these people where was this guy, where was this one, about people up the road, and then they would ask me to admit that I with my truck brought weapons into Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you with your truck bring weapons into Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you told them no, did the beatings stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During these beatings how many times were you beaten until you were almost unconscious?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you that but, for me, it seemed like an eternity.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you would leave the room after these beatings and come into the hallway, what would happen to you in the hallway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was even worse than the room.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What would happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had to go down the stairs and this is, they waited for us like the five or six soldiers, the same ones that took us upstairs, and the same people that were at the entrance. While we were going down the stairs -- this was an art of going down the stairs, and many people fell victims there at the entrance of the building.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What would happen as people tried to go down the stairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would first hit from the back, in the back, by feet, so people would fall on the first landing. This is where they caught up with the person, and then they would kick him down the stairs until the exit, and then in the corner where the stairs begin and where this first interrogation room is. This is where many people ended up, had their last moments.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you talk about going down the stairs, are you talking about the stairs that are in the location of that rounded portion of the administration building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly in that round part.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of injuries or bruising did you suffer as a result of these beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had no bones broken at that time, but I was bruised. I could not be more bruised than I was. It is hard to describe. I was completely bruised, my chest my legs. I cannot even talk about the back because I did not see them; other people saw my back. Here I could see this part of my body and it was black. We almost knew it was rotten after the beatings.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, what part of your body were you touching when you said this part of your body you were black? What part of your body is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kidneys.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any type of medical care after these beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From my colleagues. My colleague gave me his wet t-shirt and they put it around this area.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did the camp personnel ever provide you with any type of medical care after these beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody did that other than my friends, inmates.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who were the people who beat you in the interrogation rooms and then in the hallways as you left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were all Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held out on the pista at Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I spent there about three weeks.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were on the pista, how long would you be kept on the pista itself each day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were there from the dawn until the dark. I could say from dark to dark.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So from just before dawn until it became dark again at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from dawn, when it was dawning they would take us out and then when it started becoming dark they would bring us in.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you sleep at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I slept in the canteen.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say the canteen, do you refer to the restaurant portion of the administration building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is a restaurant where we went to have lunch.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the day while you were being held on the pista, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were mostly there facing down lying on our stomachs. We had to lie down the whole day. We could not even raise our heads or even get up. Sometimes they let us sit down depending on the guards. Sometimes they would let us drink this water that was there on the side.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were on the pista lying down on your stomach, in what direction would your head be facing - toward the hangar building or back toward the administration building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Toward the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you lay on your stomach in that position, how would you position your face? Would your face be faced down to the concrete or would you have your face turned to the left or the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the left and to the right.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were lying face down with your face turned either to the left or to the right, were you able to see people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we could always see people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now while you were laying out on the pista area, how many people would you estimate were also out on the pista with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe around 300, 400 people were there. That is what I think, 300 to 400 people. I cannot tell exactly. The pista was full. I did not have an opportunity to count for sure and I cannot exactly remember the groups, and there were 30 groups usually going out to lunch. But there were many of us there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you would be lying there at the pista on your stomach, would there be any areas between these rows of people, any areas where guards could walk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not an organised group, but we normally had one row and then a second row and I cannot tell you what was the distance between the rows.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So would you have two rows together and then some type of open space and then another two rows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Let me tell you. We were lying like sardines from the hangar. There was a row there and then a row here, and this is how it was up until the restaurant building.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there any area at all on this pista where the guards could walk among you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If they wanted to. If they came by people would automatically make space for them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you taken once you left the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took me -- actually I did this myself -- to the administration building, to the right. There was an entrance by the garage.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until the end of my stay in Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have testified about the beatings that you suffered during the interrogations. After the interrogations were you ever beaten again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During my stay or while I was interrogated again?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During your stay in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was on a daily basis, but not too much, passing by sort of, as the guards would pass by. Depending on the mood they would hit us, but we would just keep silent and go on.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Omarska camp did you ever personally observe others in the camp being beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of these other people who were beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At one time they were in room No. 15, I remember that well, and then I remember when they started beating Beganovic at the entrance to the white house. This is what I remember the best.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Beganovic and these others that you saw being beaten, to your knowledge what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Beganovic was a Muslim and the others, there was a group of Croats, maybe three or four, I cannot remember exactly, they might have been brothers. First they had to beat themselves and they refused to do that, and they were beating them there. We had to lie down on the pista, and we did not even try to look and see what was happening and then I never saw those people again.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The other people in addition to this incident, the other people that you saw beaten at Omarska, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was a Muslim, Beganovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: But in addition to this incident, were there other times you saw detainees beaten at Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could see beatings every day, every day. They were mostly Muslims in the camp and there were some Croats, but they were mostly Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These beatings that you saw, who were the ones who were doing the beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The guards would be coming and beating, people who were coming there for a visit. Inspectors beat us too, inspectors who would be conducting interrogations and, so to speak, almost anybody who wanted and who felt like it could beat us.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Omarska camp did you ever see detainees taken away at night and never return after they were taken away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the day, day was mostly used for beating us, but the nights were terrible for us. Nobody could sleep. We could not sleep because they were calling out people every night, and those people that were called out, some were beaten, but most of those that were called out, they never came back.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of these people who were called out at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were too many.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Of the ones that you knew, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These men who would be taken out at night, who would take them out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Guards who were there on duty.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Omarska camp did you ever see any corpses in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of those corpses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We saw many corpses. I recognised my brother's corpse.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall when it was that you saw your brother's body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was after the second interrogation or the first time when I was beaten. This is the first time when I came out to the pista. I was at the restaurant and I spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see your brother's body on the same day, this Monday, that you were first beaten or did you see it the next morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I believe you indicated you were in the restaurant when you saw your brother, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw your brother, where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him in front of the restaurant on a green area, on the grassy area. He was lying there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At first I did not know that. I was not paying attention. I did not even see because I was beaten up, and then I was told that my brother died there and he was taken out there. They took me there and showed me and then I could see.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This was your brother Dalija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could please stand up and take the pointer, and if you could show the court where it was that you saw your brother's body. If you could step toward me, please. If you could step toward me so that the Judges may see. If you could please point to where you saw your brother's body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would note that the witness is pointing to an area at the very edge of the model beyond the end of the restaurant portion of the administration building, and just a small way into the grass from the concrete area. Thank you, Mr. Hrnic. If you would please resume your seat. Sir, while you were at Omarska camp, did you ever see corpses taken away from the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How often would you see this done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was every morning. Every night we could hear that. It was mostly done early in the morning they would drive them away, but it was mostly on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were these bodies transported from the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question, I am sorry?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were these bodies transported from the camp, what type of vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A tannish, yellow colour with a double driver's area. Then the loading area was open and we could see it every morning.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where would you be when you saw these bodies being transported from the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could see easily from the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What would be the location of these bodies that you saw transported from the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Usually they were where I showed you where my brother was lying, and sometimes they were carrying them out above the white house. I do not know from this side, this is, I could see this side that I was facing, looking at it from the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time if I could have this document which is document Z3 20-7 called up on the computer, and also if the Registrar could mark this the next Prosecution Exhibit in order which is I believe 232. Sir, as you look at this photograph Prosecution Exhibit 232 for identification, does this show the type of vehicle that you saw transporting bodies from Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 232 for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 232 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it might be an appropriate time to break for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, at some stage of these proceedings could you introduce a floor plan of the hangar, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow at 10 a.m.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (The court adjourned until the following day).

procedural_notes.text: (The court adjourned for a short time)
